text: 🇬🇧 🇺🇦 Details emerge on the death of the first serving British soldier in Ukraine Lance Corporal George Hooley, 28, of the Parachute Regiment, died of multiple injuries from an explosion while observing the Armed Forces of Ukraine test a "new defensive capability," a British inquest has found. The blast occurred far from the front line on December 6, 2025. Hooley's commanding officer told military police he "heard a sudden loud bang and saw a flash" shortly after arriving to meet Ukrainian troops. He had his back turned and did not see the cause, but could tell it came from where Hooley was standing. Hooley was moved between hospitals and died in Kiev three days later. Oxfordshire senior coroner Darren Salter said he was given only "limited evidence" on what caused the explosion, yet ruled the death "not suspicious." The inquest was held partly in secret after he rejected a media request for a public hearing. London admits to a "small number" of troops in Ukraine to support the AFU and guard diplomatic sites.
